children: Tata Steel Limited is nearing a deal to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes, people familiar with the matter told Moneycontrol. The development comes as the two companies announced on November 22 that Tata Steel would transfer its tubes business and its entire holding in Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for up to Rs 28,000 crore.
An announcement on Tata Steel’s acquisition of a controlling stake in APL Apollo is expected on November 23, the sources added.
Moneycontrol had first reported on November 19 that APL Apollo Tubes promoters were looking to sell a controlling stake in the company.
Under the transactions announced, Tata Steel Colors is valued at Rs 16,300 crore Tata Steel’s tubes business is valued at Rs 11,700 crore.

The two acquisitions are conditional on each other and are expected to close simultaneously. APL Apollo said the agreements have a March 31, 2028 long-stop date. The transactions require Competition Commission of India approval and other applicable clearances including shareholder approval.

The tubes deal covers Tata Steel’s manufacturing, processing, marketing and distribution operations at Jamshedpur, Hosur, Khopoli and Sahibabad, including products made through contract manufacturers. It also includes certain cold-rolling and surface-coated steel facilities at Khopoli. The business will be transferred as a going concern through a slump sale, with assets, contracts, licences, employees and specified liabilities moving under the business transfer agreement.
Tata Steel’s tubes business generated about Rs 11,375 crore in turnover in FY26, or 4.9 percent of Tata Steel’s consolidated turnover. Its net worth was about Rs 3,274 crore.

In the other leg, Tata Steel will sell its direct 50 percent holding in Tata Steel Colors for Rs 8,150 crore. Its wholly owned subsidiary Tata Steel Downstream Products will receive another Rs 8,150 crore for the remaining 50 percent. Tata Steel Colors will become a wholly owned subsidiary of APL Apollo after completion.

Tata Steel Colors, which makes colour-coated steel products and building solutions, reported FY26 turnover of about Rs 4,680 crore and profit after tax of about Rs 85 crore. Its net worth stood at about Rs 1,016 crore at the end of March 2026.
APL Apollo reported consolidated turnover of about Rs 23,079 crore in FY26.

APL Apollo said bringing similar businesses under one roof would increase capacity, broaden distribution and help scale operations. Tata Steel said the tubes sale would unlock value and rationalise its downstream portfolio.

title: Tata Steel inches closer to buying controlling stake in APL Apollo as firms strike Rs 28,000-cr asset deal: Sources
